title: When you delete a redundant implementation, move its regression tests onto the survivor
statement: Consolidating two implementations of a defence must not drop the deleted one's tests — re-point them at the remaining path so the invariant they guarded still fails loudly. Write the migration rationale into the test file header.

title: Gate tour anchors with a data-driven drift test over the REAL registry
statement: Walk the imported TOUR_REGISTRY, scan src/ once, accept verbatim or template-prefix + quoted literal matches, and make the failure message name the fix — all eight Obsidian Brain anchors had drifted undetected before this gate.

title: Standardize a three-line Zustand slice harness and reuse it verbatim
statement: set/get closure + createXSlice(set,get,{}) + merge — no store, no provider, no Tauri bridge. Five slice test files reuse the identical harness and cross-reference each other by name.

title: Assert render cost with a spied expensive leaf and a hook-based render counter
statement: Turn render cost into an assertion: mock the expensive leaf (MarkdownRenderer) to a countable spy, wrap a hook every component calls to tick a render counter, and budget-assert perKeystroke <= 8, < mounted/3, AND > 0 as a sanity floor — with an anti-freeze pair asserting changed content STILL re-parses ("memo must be a cache, not a freeze").

title: Test a rebuild's cost and correctness against the legacy implementation as oracle
statement: When rebuilding hot logic, keep the old implementation verbatim in the test as an oracle, spy on the allocation itself (parse call counts, storage write lengths), and property-test total ordering over shuffled inputs with deliberate ties. Micro: RFC3339 is fixed-width ASCII so `<`/`>` IS collation — drop localeCompare in hot comparators.

title: Pin store race fixes by interleaving a deferred promise with the competing mutation
statement: Slice-level concurrency bugs are testable without rendering: wire set/get around a plain object as a minimal store harness, drive the API mock with a manually-resolved deferred, start the fetch, run the competing mutation, then resolve — and assert the ghost row does not come back.

title: Bridge fire-and-forget eval harnesses with a window global plus a hidden DOM result stash
statement: When a test harness can inject JS but cannot await a promise across calls (fire-and-forget /eval), expose a dev-gated `window.__x.dispatch(action)` that ALSO mirrors every settled result into a hidden DOM node (`data-testid` stash) a later /query call reads back. Gate on `import.meta.env.DEV` so the global never ships; mount/unmount the bridge with the surface it drives so it exists exactly while something can answer.

title: Name each in-memory SQLite test database per test — shared-cache memory URIs are process-wide
statement: A bare file::memory:?cache=shared is ONE database for the whole process, and libtest runs tests in parallel — so tests that look isolated share tables and flake. Give every test its own named memory DB (unique name per test) and the isolation is real again.

title: Replace sleeps with deadline-bounded predicate polls that embed the last observed state in the failure
statement: Async/streaming UI is waited on by looping to a deadline over a cheap state snapshot, returning on match, else throwing an error that embeds the last snapshot — so a timeout failure tells you what the UI actually was. Equally important: write down which built-in wait is unsafe for which element class (here, the harness's /wait visibility check is offsetParent !== null, always null for position:fixed panels).

title: A build-acceleration cache must never be able to fail the build
statement: Wiring a compilation cache (sccache, remote cache) as an unconditional wrapper makes the cache's availability a build dependency: a cache-backend outage kills every compile before it starts. Probe the cache's health in a dedicated step and enable the wrapper only on success — degrade to a slow build with a warning, never to no build.

title: A CI gate that dies before its verdict has never gated anything — audit that each gate actually runs
statement: CI steps fail in ways that look like enforcement but check nothing: a step that errors before reaching its assertion, a command masked with `|| true`, a flag omission that silently skips the surface under test, or a trigger that never fires on the real development flow. Periodically verify each gate has produced a genuine red at least once, and treat 'this step has never actually run' as a distinct bug class.

title: In an iterative agent loop, run only the required gates per iteration and batch informational gates into one final pass
statement: Split verification gates into required (they gate area completion) and informational (they only decorate the report). Run required gates after every iteration, and run the informational set exactly once after the loop ends. Rerunning a slow build or advisory audit after each of ~70 iterations burns hours of wall-clock on results that change nothing.

title: Test against a real migrated database and control time by writing it
statement: A mocked store drifts from the real schema, and tests that sleep to exercise aging or expiry logic are slow and flaky. Spin a fresh temp-directory database per test through the full migration chain, so the migrations themselves stay covered, and make time deterministic by writing explicit timestamps into rows rather than waiting for the clock. One integration file per storage-backed subsystem keeps the failures legible.

title: Match the test pool's concurrency shape to production's
statement: In-memory test doubles quietly change concurrency semantics: a shared-cache in-memory database deadlocks a second connection under a write transaction where a file-backed pool would not. Choose the pool shape per test according to what the module under test actually does — serialize to a single connection for transactional code, share the cache when the calls are single-statement — and write the reason down at the point of use. Anything held in process-wide state needs an explicit test lock plus a reset, or tests contaminate each other only under parallelism.

title: Gate evals on curated fixtures: hard zero-tolerance, soft baselines
statement: An evaluation harness that only reports scores never blocks anything, and one that hard-gates every metric blocks on noise. Seed hand-curated gold fixtures per concern and run the real stage code against them, standing in an oracle only for the genuinely non-deterministic judgement. Split the gates: correctness and safety properties are unconditional zero-tolerance, while quality metrics compare against a committed baseline with a bounded regression tolerance that must be recalibrated deliberately, never silently.

title: Keep eval aggregation pure and preserve explicit nulls in fixtures
statement: An evaluation harness has its own arithmetic — averaging, exclusion, ranking, collision resolution — and that arithmetic can be wrong while every model call succeeds. Put it in pure functions over the generated types so it is testable without running a model. Then watch the fixture builders: reading overrides with a nullish fallback silently converts an explicit null into the default, which is precisely the case the null-exclusion tests exist to check.

title: Gate theme contrast in CI, hard-failing only on text tokens
statement: Accessibility loses when it is a style opinion argued in review, so turn it into a check: parse the theme stylesheet, resolve each theme's effective variable map with overrides layered on the root, and compute contrast for the pairs that matter. Hard-fail only on the tokens that carry readable copy — and check them at the minimum opacity your captions actually use, since a token that passes at full opacity can fail as rendered. Keep accent and status colours as informational warnings so the gate stays credible.

title: Assert VALUES in wire round-trip tests — positional encoding reorders silently
statement: MessagePack encodes enum variants positionally, so a field reordered in the enum silently reinterprets the payload. Round-trip every frame in tests asserting every field's value, including both shapes of an optional-bearing variant.

title: Pin a two-renderer prompt contract with a test naming every deserializer field
statement: When a prompt has two renderers (in-app and dispatched), pin the contract with a test that names every field the deserializer expects, so drift between them is caught at test time.

title: Share ONE pure renderer between in-process and out-of-process paths
statement: The daemon-rendered prompt is byte-identical to the windowed one for the same data — a regression appears in both paths and is caught by either test.

title: Pin code-config to locale-catalog parity with a key-set equality test
statement: When a code map is the single source of truth for both a visual attribute and an i18n token key (verdict -> accent + token), add a unit test asserting the map's token-key set equals the catalog section's key set exactly — a value added to one side but not the other then fails CI instead of degrading silently to an unstyled fallback badge or a raw untranslated token.

title: Lock a data catalog's file shape and its cross-language seed idempotency in one test
statement: For data-as-config catalogs, one vitest can pin all three layers: read the on-disk JSON and assert its exact keys, assert the accessor surfaces it, and grep the other language's seed source for the idempotency idioms (INSERT OR IGNORE, existence pre-check) — pinning 'works on fresh install' and 'works on upgrade' without any migration machinery.

title: Seed schedule previews with the same id the engine hashes so preview and reality agree
statement: When a scheduler expands hash-based tokens (Jenkins-style `H` in cron) using a stable per-trigger seed, every preview surface must accept and pass the SAME seed (the trigger id) — otherwise the preview shows a different minute than the engine will actually fire, and the calendar lies. Syntax-only previews before an id exists may omit the seed; anything shown as 'next runs' must not. Windowed projections carry an explicit backend-capped max.

title: A mock seam may replace the slow producer, never the wiring under test — and assert the mock's own sequence
statement: The mock build walks the store through the actual phase sequence so the real event bus emits the real completion events and the flow completes through its genuine contract — explicitly not via an emit shortcut. The spec asserts the driven phase list itself, so the mock cannot silently drift from the real stream.

title: Lock-step tests pin two hand-maintained lists against each other, and one test per module runs against the real schema
statement: When an allowlist and its embedded copies (or seeds and their consumers) are maintained by hand in two places, add a test that walks both and asserts set-equality — the drift it catches had made every ingest permanently report missing files. Separately, when most tests build their own tables, they all stay green if production's migration stops creating the index they exercise; each such module carries one test that runs against the real migration, with the incident (a sibling device dropped the FTS table, correctly at the time) recorded next to it.

title: Mirror fixture lists in both suites of a cross-language contract
statement: When the same classification ladder or enum set exists in two languages, neither compiler can see the other, so the two drift and the mismatch surfaces as runtime rejection of legitimate values. Keep a fixture table in each suite that is byte-for-byte identical, with a header naming the other file, so adding a case on one side fails until the other moves. Populate it with real production shapes, since the fixture list doubles as the record of what the classifier is actually for.

title: Run one storage suite against every driver, real or faked
statement: Two storage drivers behind one interface typecheck identically and behave differently, and the differences are exactly the semantics the type signature cannot express — create-if-absent, partial merge, transactional idempotency. Write the storage tests against the interface and execute the same suite against every driver, faking the one you cannot run locally. The bugs this catches are silent data loss, not error messages.

title: A multi-driver store needs a parity suite, not a shared interface
statement: A shared storage interface makes every driver typecheck, which is exactly why teams stop there and ship divergent semantics. The interface cannot express create-if-absent, partial merge, or transactional idempotency, so those differences surface only as data loss in whichever environment runs the weaker driver. Treat cross-driver execution of the same suite as a required tier whenever more than one driver exists, however thin the second one is.

title: Require at least one real pass before reporting green
statement: A verification pass that reports zero failures over a set where everything was skipped — missing credentials, unsupported target — reads as success and is not one. Define the pass criterion as no failures and at least one genuine pass, and keep skips visible in the summary rather than folded into the count. Distinguish 'available at runtime' from 'actually exercised' in both the result model and the wording the user reads.

title: Keep test and mock data out of surfaces users read as truth
statement: Two leaks share one rule. Instrumentation that promotes rows into incident, health or metric tables must be a no-op during test, lab, eval and simulation runs, or evaluation traffic corrupts the operational picture it is supposed to measure. And a pane with no real data source yet must render empty rather than placeholder rows — users cannot tell a mock from a fact, and once shipped the placeholder is treated as project state.

title: Assert array/row IDENTITY, not just values, for memo bail-out contracts
statement: A patch outside the loaded window must return the SAME array reference and untouched rows must keep object identity — assert `expect(h.get().tasks).toBe(before)`, because memoized consumers depend on reference stability.

title: Guard a banned dependency by asserting its absence in the module's raw source
statement: Import the module's own source with ?raw in a test and assert the forbidden dependency is ABSENT: behavioral spies only prove the tested path clean, while a raw-source assertion proves NO path can reach the banned surface. A self-check toContain prevents a silent pass on a failed import.

title: Derive exhaustiveness tests from the type's own constant and guard the guard
statement: A switch with no default returning Promise<void> lets a new kind silently no-op — so the test iterates KINDS × verdicts asserting each was honoured (the failure NAMES the kind), and a second loop guards that every kind actually had a decidable case. Fixtures export ALL_KINDS derived from the same constant; a compile-time sibling uses _AssertAllCovered & _AssertNoExtra.

title: Test accessibility rulings as absences, not just presences
statement: Accessibility rulings are tested as ABSENCES: one live region owned by the app, never the feature (assert zero [aria-live]/[role=status]/[role=alert] nodes inside the deck); identical consecutive messages must REMOUNT to be spoken twice ({text,seq} stamp, assert a different NODE); removing a region obliges saying where the fact is announced instead (byte-identical utterance asserted); no colour-only signal; depth-stacked cards get tabIndex isTop?0:-1 because pointer-events-none removes mouse but NOT tab order.

title: State a cross-domain ranking once, claims beside numbers, tested as relations
statement: Seven queues with no shared urgency scale get one explicit weight table with the claim written next to each number — including arguments against itself — and tests assert RELATIONS between bands (X above Y, never-an-incident thresholds), not magic numbers. The table is mirrored with claims in DESIGN.md, whose header records a dated rewrite and a still-true history section.

title: Pair every expensive real-LLM spec with a cheap mocked twin, and let each header name what the other covers
statement: The flagship flow exists twice: a real end-to-end spec (15-minute timeout, nightly/on-demand) and a bounded deterministic mock twin in the per-PR regression run. Each header states exactly what it does NOT cover and points at its twin, so the CI-safe structural gate and the one test that proves the real pipeline both survive — and nobody deletes either as redundant.

title: Assert the strongest available signal — backend truth or a re-run of the real thing — and pre-assert the fixture fails
statement: Do not trust an agent's claim or a plausible DOM: re-execute the real verification (run the failing test under the runtime and assert exit 0), and pre-assert the fixture actually fails before dispatch so a broken fixture cannot produce a vacuous pass. Where a UI action has a backend consequence, make the backend state the load-bearing assertion and demote DOM changes to implementation detail; snapshot pre-existing entity ids so assertions read what THIS run created.

title: Write serialization down as an architectural constraint with the named future fix, not a flake workaround
statement: workers: 1 and retries: 0 each carry a recorded justification (a singleton backend session would be corrupted by parallel specs; a real-LLM failure usually has a real cause), and the README names the correct future fix — per-test session ids, not multi-worker hacks — which stops the next contributor from bumping workers to chase speed. Long default timeouts are likewise defended in writing: a flaky test is worse than a slow one.

title: Write the contract as numbered points and pin each with a test
statement: For predicates whose edge cases are the whole product — time windows, dedupe intervals, boundary inclusivity — scattered example tests leave the semantics written nowhere. Write the contract once as numbered points in the module documentation and give each point a matching property test whose name cites it, so a failing test is a contract change requiring an explicit doc edit rather than a puzzle. Example-based tests then only need to cover the memorable cases.

title: Document the canonical test pattern and an exhaustive deviation list
statement: When two test styles coexist for historical reasons, leaving the choice to taste guarantees both keep growing. Name one as canonical with concrete template files, state why it is canonical, and enumerate the only valid reasons to deviate — closing with the fact that anything not on the list is not a deviation but a default-pattern test. Use the same document to mandate the categories people skip, such as persistence-migration tests that only break for users with old stored state.

title: Measure coverage on logic layers and ratchet the floor
statement: A repo-wide coverage percentage measures mostly presentational code and turns the gate into a number nobody trusts. Scope the measurement to the logic core — libraries, feature logic, route handlers — excluding presentational components, barrels and vendored code, so the figure means something. Then pin the thresholds just under the current measured value so the gate blocks a regression without demanding a coverage big-bang, and raise them as real work lands.

title: Layer the test surface by what only that layer can catch
statement: A single test tier always over-serves one risk and misses another, so decide the layers deliberately rather than accumulating them. Fast unit tests cover pure logic and constrain the runner choice (pick one that can import your server-guarded modules), browser-driven suites cover journeys, and separate configurations keep functional checks apart from user-acceptance journeys. Model-dependent behaviour needs its own evaluation lane, because a pass/fail assertion is the wrong instrument for output quality.

title: Inject ports to make untestable branches testable, and document the asymmetries
statement: Injected ports make an untestable branch testable, with the contract stated as an invariant: "Every decision either DEFERS, or WRITES, or THROWS. Never nothing." Port asymmetries are each justified rather than smoothed — split apply/decline, omitted tokens named as deliberate, ordering with stated residual, Promise.all chosen so one failure reaches the caller, and deep-links that write nothing still THROW when the route is absent.

title: Give background-ticker cutoffs a three-tier override: env test knob > user tune > default
statement: Every time-based cutoff in a background loop should resolve through an explicit precedence chain — env var for test harnesses, clamped user setting, built-in default — and the transition rules themselves should be pure functions so the timing logic is unit-testable without running the loop.

title: One-shot deterministic layout: bounded force pass, no clock or RNG, hashed tie-breaks, pinned anchors
statement: Auto-layout ('tidy') runs a BOUNDED force-directed pass once and snaps to the result — no continuous simulation. Determinism is a hard invariant: no Date, no Math.random anywhere; inputs are sorted; the only tie-break for coincident points is a stable string hash — so identical input always yields identical output (testable, reproducible, diffable). User-pinned nodes are anchors: they exert forces but never move, and when overlap resolution meets two pinned nodes it leaves them alone — the user's explicit layout wins. Overlap resolution is itself a bounded pass (cap on iterations, whole shove onto the free end when one node is pinned).

title: Add a named-method RPC seam plus state injectors, so UI states are tested without burning an LLM turn
statement: On a fire-and-forget eval channel, dispatch to named methods on a window-scoped test object and await a JSON response; on top of that seam expose state injectors (force streaming, set messages, set cards, set flags) so render-tier behavior — streaming phase labels, marker dividers, card widgets — is asserted deterministically instead of via a 30-90s model turn. The highest-leverage split for testing any LLM-driven app: 'does the model do the right thing' vs 'does the UI render each state correctly'.

title: Unit-test the E2E harness's own pure fixture logic, because the E2E run can never be a per-PR gate
statement: When an E2E harness contains decisions (which questions to seed, what placeholder to invent), extract that logic into a pure module and cover it with fast unit tests that DO run per-PR — guarding specific past bugs the live run cannot cheaply re-check. Keep the fixture module the single source of truth shared by the spec and any driver scripts so they cannot diverge.

title: Asserting on styling-class substrings couples tests to cosmetics — plant data attributes and migrate the query seam
statement: When the harness's query endpoint returns className but not arbitrary attributes, specs end up discriminating UI state by CSS token (a color class means done, a width class means compact) — breaking on cosmetic refactors while asserting nothing behavioral. The fix is data-status/data-* attributes plus a query seam that returns them; the codebase is mid-migration, preferring an attribute reader and falling back to class scanning. Sibling smells: hand-synced registry copies and specs reaching into the bridge's private members via casts.

title: Guard server-only modules at runtime and inject their deps lazily
statement: Marking a module server-only with a build-time package makes it unresolvable to lightweight test runners, so the modules that most need protection become the ones with no unit tests. Use a tiny runtime assertion instead, and have each module reach its real infrastructure through a lazily-imported defaults function passed as an optional last parameter. The same module is then both the production wiring and a pure, injectable unit with no mocking framework — and re-reading config per call keeps a rotated key effective without a restart.

title: Keep business logic pure and inject the provider seam
statement: Logic that hard-imports an LLM client or a database can only be tested by mocking modules, which couples the suite to the wiring rather than the behaviour. Write the logic as pure functions over plain data, taking any external capability as an injected interface so production passes the real one and tests pass a fake function. Where the behaviour under test is the query itself, use a real in-memory database rather than a mock query layer, so the SQL stays covered.

title: Extract framework-free predicates out of middleware plumbing
statement: Gating decisions written inside framework middleware can only be tested by booting the framework's runtime, so in practice they are not tested at all. Extract the decision into a pure predicate over a small explicit input type with no framework imports, and reduce the middleware to request and response plumbing that calls it. Ordering the rules explicitly in that predicate is what makes fail-open and fail-closed cases reviewable.

title: Write policy decisions as pure functions over plain data
statement: Policy — route gating, provider ordering, access scope, output quality — is the part of a system most worth testing and the part most often entangled with I/O and SDK imports. Express each decision as a dependency-free function over plain data with the clock and any config passed in, and keep the framework and network calls strictly outside it. Independently converged on by several projects in this portfolio, which makes it a candidate workspace-wide default rather than a local preference.

title: Move a component's computation into a React-free sibling module
statement: When the interesting part of a component is a computation — bucketing, faceting, scoring, smoothing, reachability — testing it through the component means booting a DOM to assert arithmetic. Put the computation in a plain module beside the component, generic over the row type via injected accessors so it knows nothing about the feature's shapes, and unit-test it directly while the component keeps only rendering. The payoff is what becomes cheap to assert: hysteresis bands, deep facet trees, gating rules.
